title: Protocol for photoactivation of YAP in cancer cell spheroids embedded in collagen gels
protocol: Place 150 μl of collagen Type I solution (8.35 mg/mL) per well in an Eppendorf tube on ice.
Prepare NaOH solution by mixing 2.5 μL NaOH (1 M) with 47.5 μL PBS per well in an Eppendorf tube on ice.
Combine collagen and NaOH solutions, mix gently.
Apply 200 μl of combined solution to each well of an 8-well slide.
Collect spheroids and surrounding medium from a low adhesion 96-well plate using disposable plastic pipettes.
Add two collected spheroids with their medium (total volume including collagen solution should be 400 μL) to each well of the 8-well slide.
Mix gel gently after adding spheroids, if necessary.
Place 8-well slide in incubator at 37°C/5% CO2 for 30 min.
Check presence and shape of embedded spheroids in light microscope.
Ensure spheroids are not damaged before proceeding to next step.
Add correct amount of NaOH to control pH of the ensuing gel.
Maintain final pH at 7.4 for optimal conditions.
Keep collagen at low temperatures to prevent immediate gel formation.
Ensure proper handling and properties of the gel during experiments.
Adjust the volume of collagen solution added to yield a final concentration of 3.13 mg/mL in each well.
Use slow pipetting and avoid narrow pipette tips when handling spheroids.
Ensure the pH is maintained within physiological range during preparation.
Perform additional standard viability tests on spheroids without interfering with the final readout.
Mix 1 μg of optoYAP plasmid with 1 μg of PAG plasmid.
Add 3 μL of Xtreme Gene 9 transfection reagent to the mixture.
Fill up to a total volume of 100 μL with Optimem.
Carefully mix by tapping the tube.
Incubate for 20 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Use 10 μL of the transfection mixture per well for an 8-well slide.
Add 3 μL of photocaged lysine per well (final concentration: 0.75 μg/μL).
Incubate for at least 24 h at 37°C/5% CO2 before proceeding to the next major step.
Seed cells on an 8-well slide at a desired concentration, such as 5000 cells per well.
Exchange medium for DMEM without FBS and with 1% PenStrep.
Wait 24–48 hours for cells to settle and adjust to new medium.
Transfect cells as described above.
Perform experiments.
Add 50 μL of matrigel to each well of an 8-well slide.
Carefully spread the matrigel until the entire well is covered with a pipette tip.
Incubate the well plate for 30 minutes at 37°C/5% CO2.
Carefully seed cells on top of the gel as usual (e.g., 5000 cells per well).
Incubate for 24 hours.
Transfect cells as described above.
Activate optoYAP using a 365 nm UV lamp for general activation in spheroids.
Use a 365 nm laser or LED and microscope for site-selective activation of optoYAP.
Illuminate the desired area of the spheroid for 20 seconds at 0.6 mW/mm².
Incubate the activated areas for 72 hours at 37°C/5% CO₂.
Remove the medium from the wells carefully with a pipette.
Fix the spheroids with 200 μL of 4% formaldehyde for 40 minutes in the wells.
Wash the fixed spheroids twice with 300 μL cold PBS for 20 minutes each time.
Permeabilize cells with 200 μL of 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 20 minutes.
Wash the permeabilized cells with 300 μL PBS for 30 minutes.
Block the cells with 200 μL PBS containing 1% BSA overnight (10–24 hours).
Dilute 1 μg of primary antibodies in 200 μL PBS containing 1% BSA.
Add diluted antibodies to the cells and incubate for 72 hours.
Wash twice with 300 μL cold PBS for 20 min each.
Incubate for 48 h with 1 μg secondary antibodies in 200 μL PBS containing 1% BSA.
Wash with 300 μL cold PBS for 20 min.
Stain with a 0.5 μg/mL solution of Hoechst in PBS for 40 min.
Wash with 300 μL cold PBS for 30 min.
Renew PBS and assure sample remains wet during storage.
Prevent drying to ensure samples remain stable at 4°C for months if protected from light.
Use non-illuminated spheroids as negative controls.
Use cells on plastic substrates or spheroids transfected with YAP fused to a nuclear localization sequence as positive controls.
